The cosine sum is not zero, so the claimed answer is wrong.

The setup is right: the ten terms pair up as $k=1,\dots,10$, and each product equals $\tfrac12\left[\cos\tfrac{\pi}{6}-\cos\tfrac{(4k+2)\pi}{24}\right]$. The error is the claim that $\sum_{k=1}^{10}\cos\tfrac{(4k+2)\pi}{24}=0$. The angles are $\tfrac{\pi}{24}\cdot\{6,10,14,\dots,42\}$, with cosines $0.7071,\ 0.2588,\ -0.2588,\ -0.7071,\ -0.9659,\ -0.9659,\ -0.7071,\ -0.2588,\ 0.2588,\ 0.7071$. These sum to $-2\cos\tfrac{\pi}{12}\approx -1.9319$, not $0$.

Correct value: $S=\tfrac12\left[5\sqrt3+2\cos\tfrac{\pi}{12}\right]=\tfrac{5\sqrt3}{2}+\tfrac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{4}\approx 5.296$.

A direct numerical evaluation of the ten original products also gives $\approx 5.296$, while $\tfrac{5\sqrt3}{2}\approx 4.330$.
